case_types.name: Patent: district court and ITC
case_types.side_a: Patent owner (incl. exclusive licensee, ITC complainant)
case_types.side_b: Accused infringer (incl. declaratory-judgment plaintiff, ITC respondent)

case_types.name: Patent: PTAB trials (IPR, PGR, CBM) and inter partes reexams
case_types.note: If the PTO intervenes, it is not treated as a side.

case_types.name: Patent: ex parte appeals and ex parte reexams
case_types.note: Always shown filtered by forum, so these never mix with IPR or district-court results.

case_types.name: Trademark
case_types.side_b: Opposer, cancellation petitioner, PTO, or accused infringer

case_types.name: Federal employment (MSPB, arbitrator, OCWR, back-pay claims)
Government contracts (boards, CFC, bid protests)
case_types.side_b: Government (plus the intervening awardee in a bid protest)

case_types.name: Other Court of Federal Claims (takings, tax, military pay, vaccine, misc.)
Trade: antidumping/countervailing duties
case_types.note: Sides defined by duty outcome, not by party, because Commerce may have ruled either way.

case_types.name: Other petitions against an agency (DOJ, GAO, etc.)

issues.covers: Whether the claims are directed to patent-eligible subject matter (Alice/Mayo), incl. §101 decided on the pleadings.
Whether a single prior-art reference discloses every claim limitation.
Whether the claims would have been obvious, incl. motivation to combine, reasonable expectation of success and objective indicia.
Whether the specification shows possession of the claimed invention.
Whether the specification enables the full scope of the claims without undue experimentation.
Whether the claims are reasonably certain, incl. means-plus-function claims lacking corresponding structure.
Whether a reference or activity qualifies as prior art (printed publication, on-sale bar, public use) or the claims are entitled to an earlier date.
Whether claims are invalid over the patentee's own earlier patent.
Correct inventorship, correction under §256, and derivation-type inventorship disputes.
Validity of reissue claims, the recapture rule, and certificates of correction.
Meaning of disputed claim terms, coded by its effect on the judgment (e.g. a vacated noninfringement judgment favors the patent owner).
Whether the accused product or process meets every limitation, incl. §271(e) and extraterritoriality.
Infringement by equivalents and limits on it (prosecution history estoppel, dedication-disclosure, vitiation).
Liability for inducing or contributing to infringement, and joint/divided infringement.
Whether the patent is unenforceable for misconduct before the PTO or in litigation.
Defenses based on a license, patent exhaustion, laches or equitable estoppel.
Reasonable royalty, lost profits, apportionment, damages experts, marking and notice (§287).
Willful infringement findings and enhanced damages under §284.
Preliminary and permanent injunctions (eBay factors, likelihood of success).
Contract disputes over patent licenses, royalties, assignments and title.

issues.issue: Institution, time bar, real party in interest
issues.covers: Reviewability of institution, the §315(b) time bar, real-party-in-interest and related threshold rulings.
Whether a petitioner is estopped from raising grounds it raised or reasonably could have raised, at the Board or in court.

issues.issue: Motions to amend and substitute claims
issues.covers: Whether the Board properly denied or granted amendment of claims during a trial.
Domestic industry (technical and economic prongs), importation, and other Section 337 requirements.
DuPont factors and whether the mark is likely to cause confusion with another mark, incl. priority of use when decided as part of a §2(d) claim (opposition or cancellation).
Whether the mark is merely descriptive, generic, or has acquired distinctiveness.
Functionality, failure to function, §2(a)-(c) bars, geographic descriptiveness or misdescriptiveness.
Fraud on the PTO, abandonment, and nonuse as grounds to cancel a registration.

issues.issue: Interpretation of benefit statutes and regulations
issues.covers: Meaning of a Title 38 statute or VA regulation (a question of law within the court's review).
Legal standards for service connection, including presumptive conditions (e.g. herbicide exposure).
The date from which benefits are payable.
Whether a final VA decision contains CUE warranting revision.

issues.issue: Duty to assist, notice, benefit of the doubt
issues.covers: VA's procedural duties to the claimant and the benefit-of-the-doubt rule.
Whether the agency proved the charge and nexus to the efficiency of the service.
Whether the penalty was reasonable under the Douglas factors.
Protected disclosure, contributing factor, and the agency's clear-and-convincing defense.
Discrimination affirmative defenses, USERRA and VEOA claims.
Entitlement to FERS/CSRS retirement, disability retirement or survivor annuities.

issues.issue: Due process and harmful procedural error
issues.covers: Whether the employee received required process and whether a procedural error was harmful.
Back Pay Act, FLSA, locality and other pay claims by federal employees.
Meaning of contract terms and the parties' obligations.
Whether the procurement decision was arbitrary or unlawful and whether the protester was prejudiced.
Whether a termination was proper and its consequences.
Certification, sum certain, same-claim and other CDA claim requirements.
Amount recoverable, equitable adjustments, and defenses such as sovereign acts or accord and satisfaction.
Physical and regulatory takings, incl. rails-to-trails cases.
Federal tax refund suits.
Military pay, wrongful discharge and military disability retirement claims.
Whether the vaccine caused the injury (Althen) or a Table injury is shown.
Vaccine Act timeliness, procedure and other non-causation issues.
Illegal exaction, judicial pay, tribal trust and other Tucker Act money claims.
Commerce's methodology for dumping margins and subsidy rates.
Whether Commerce properly applied adverse facts available and the rate selected.
Whether a product falls within the scope of an antidumping or countervailing duty order.
ITC material injury and threat determinations.
Correct tariff classification of imported goods.
Valuation, country of origin, drawback and protest issues.
Lawfulness of presidential or agency tariff actions.
Appellate jurisdiction, finality, mootness, the tribunal's own jurisdiction, and the limits on review of veterans' cases (§7292).
Article III and statutory standing, incl. standing to appeal a PTAB decision.
Filing deadlines, statutes of limitation, equitable tolling, and laches outside patent cases.
Whether an argument was preserved below or on appeal.
Res judicata and collateral estoppel, incl. preclusion from PTAB decisions. Side = whoever invoked it.
Inadequate reasoning, failure to address an argument, new grounds of rejection, notice.
Appointments Clause, due process, Seventh Amendment and similar challenges.
Rule 12(b)(6) plausibility for claims other than §101 eligibility.
Venue and transfer rulings, incl. on mandamus.
Discovery, evidence, sanctions, new trial, leave to amend, class certification and similar rulings.
§285, EAJA, CDA, Vaccine Act and other fee and cost awards.
Anything not covered above; a free-text description is required. More than ~5% here in the test means a code is missing.
